E1 = Table 10 National Cloud Security Policy, E2 = Table 11 National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, E3 = Table 12 National IoT Security Policy; control_id = the annex prefix, a dash and the policy's own number. controls.title: Governance Framework
controls.description: The entity shall establish, implement, and regularly review a cloud security policy that addresses key aspects of cloud security.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall establish, implement, and regularly review a cloud security policy that addresses key aspects of cloud security. When defining the information security policy for cloud computing, the cloud service customer shall take the following into account:
• information stored in the cloud computing environment can be subject to access and management by the cloud service provider.
• assets can be maintained in the cloud computing environment, e.g. application programs.
• processes can run on a multi-tenant, virtualized cloud service.
• the cloud service users and the context in which they use the cloud service.
• the cloud service administrators of the cloud service customer who have privileged access.
• the geographical locations of the cloud service provider's organization and the countries where the cloud service provider can store the cloud service customer data (even temporarily).

controls.title: Data Governance
controls.description: The entity shall implement policies and procedures for data classification, labelling and handling throughout its’ lifecycle to secure the data that is resident (permanently or temporarily) within the service’s geographically distributed (physical and virtual) applications, infrastructure, network and systems components and shared with other third parties to ascertain any regulatory, statutory, or supply chain agreement (SLA) compliance impact.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall implement policies and procedures for data classification, labelling and handling throughout its’ lifecycle to secure the data that is resident (permanently or temporarily) within the service’s geographically distributed (physical and virtual) applications, infrastructure, network and systems components and shared with other third parties to ascertain any regulatory, statutory, or supply chain agreement (SLA) compliance impact.

The entity shall classify their data before migrating to the cloud, based on the potential impact of its compromise on operations, reputation, financial stability, and regulatory compliance and align this classification with the levels outlined in the National Cloud Security Policy.

controls.title: Encryption and Cryptography
controls.description: The entity shall establish and implement policies and procedures for the use of encryption protocols for the protection of sensitive data in storage and data in transmission as per applicable legal, statutory, and regulatory compliance obligations.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall establish and implement policies and procedures for the use of encryption protocols for the protection of sensitive data in storage and data in transmission as per applicable legal, statutory, and regulatory compliance obligations.

The entity shall ensure secure key management practices are implemented.

Partial Sovereign Cloud Requirements
Consumers shall conduct a risk assessment to determine whether Hold Your Own Key (HYOK) capabilities are required to be implemented. If the risk assessment indicates that HYOK is necessary, consumers shall implement it to retain exclusive control over encryption keys and mitigate the risk of unauthorized access to data. In cases where HYOK is implemented, consumers shall ensure that key access, revocation, and auditability are supported without dependency on the CSP.

• Applying stringent data protection controls for AI/ML data both at rest and in motion to ensure its confidentiality and integrity.

• identify and classify data collected throughout the IoT ecosystem.
• ensure, through contracts, that they are provided with clear and transparent information about how their data is being used, by whom, and for what purposes for each IoT device and service.
• ensure, through contracts, that it can exercise its rights to information, access, erasure, rectification, data portability, restriction of processing, objection to processing, and its right not to be evaluated based on automated processing; and

The entity shall ensure that contractual requirements with cloud service providers (CSPs) are formalized and agreed upon, including:
• Non-disclosure agreements.
• Service level agreements.
• Security and privacy requirements.
• Sovereignty requirements.
• Availability requirements.
• Incident reporting requirements.
• service exit requirements.
• change management requirements.
• right to audit.

Entity shall:
• avoid the collection of sensitive data.
• minimize the data collected and retained.
• restrict access to the physical and logical location of data only to authorized individuals

controls.applicability: When the entity uses IoT devices and services
obligations: Entity shall ensure IoT networks are secured by: utilizing secure ports and protocols with authentication and encryption enabled.
Entity shall ensure IoT networks are secured by: considering security controls and interoperability across different routing networks.
Entity shall ensure IoT networks are secured by: segregating IoT networks from the corporate network and implementing micro-segmentation for controlled access.
Entity shall ensure IoT networks are secured by: restricting and controlling information exchange and infrastructure management of IoT devices and applications.
Entity shall ensure IoT networks are secured by: disabling unused and default network services, protocols, and ports.
Entity shall ensure IoT networks are secured by: conducting IoT solution administration and management via a separate, segregated network.
Entity shall ensure IoT networks are secured by: employing best practice cryptography for secure communications in consumer IoT devices.

controls.title: Audit Logging
controls.description: The entity shall produce, store, protect, and analyze logs for IoT devices, systems, and applications for events such as:
controls.full_text:
The entity shall produce, store, protect, and analyze logs for IoT devices, systems, and applications for events such as:
• User logins, logouts, and unsuccessful authentication attempts.
• Connection and disconnection attempts, including unsuccessful connection attempts.
• Unsuccessful authorization attempts.
• Access to sensitive data.
• Importing and exporting data from removable media.
• Any changes in access privileges.
• Creation, modification, and deletion of data by users.
• Impactful operations.
• Remote operations.
• Security update failures.
• Physical access attempts, where possible.
• Emergency access attempts, where possible.
